items.prompt:
A student is telling her class about her pet dog. She says: 'My dog Biscuit has fluffy brown and white fur and floppy ears. He is a beagle.'

She wants to add a visual. Which is the better choice?
  A) A photograph of Biscuit showing his brown and white fur and floppy ears.
  B) A photograph of a dog food bag.

Write A or B.

steps: The description is about what Biscuit looks like: his fur color and floppy ears.
Option A shows exactly what was described — Biscuit himself.
Option B shows dog food, which has nothing to do with what Biscuit looks like.
A visual should match what the description is about.

items.prompt:
A student is describing how to make a paper airplane. He says: 'First, fold the paper in half the long way. Then fold the top two corners down to the middle. Then fold the sides in again to make the wings.'

He wants to add a visual. Which is the better choice?
  A) A photograph of an airplane flying in the sky.
  B) A step-by-step diagram showing each folding step in order.

Write A or B.

steps: The student is describing steps in a process — how to fold paper.
Option B (step-by-step diagram) shows each fold in order, which matches the description.
Option A (airplane in sky) shows a real airplane, not a paper folding process.
When describing steps, a diagram showing each step is the best visual.

items.prompt:
A student is sharing the story of going to the beach. She says: 'We went to Ocean Beach on a hot Saturday. My little brother dug a hole in the sand big enough to sit in, and the waves kept filling it up with water.'

She wants to add a visual. Which is the better choice?
  A) A drawing of her brother sitting in his sand hole while waves come in.
  B) A photograph of fish at an aquarium.

Write A or B.

steps: The story is about her brother digging a hole at the beach and waves filling it.
Option A shows exactly that scene — the hole, the waves, and the brother.
Option B shows fish at an aquarium, which has nothing to do with the beach story.
The visual should illustrate the specific story being told.

items.prompt:
A student is describing a tornado for the class. He says: 'A tornado is a spinning column of air that touches the ground. It spins very fast and can pick up trees and cars.'

He wants to add a visual. Which is the better choice?
  A) A photograph of a clear blue sky.
  B) A photograph of a real tornado with its spinning funnel shape.

Write A or B.

steps: The student is describing what a tornado looks like: a spinning column touching the ground.
Option B (real tornado photo) shows the spinning funnel shape that the student described.
Option A (clear blue sky) shows the opposite of what is being described.
The visual should show the subject of the description.

items.prompt:
A student is recounting the story of visiting her grandmother in Puerto Rico. She says: 'My grandma lives in a town called Ponce. It is in the south part of Puerto Rico, about an hour from the airport.'

She wants to add a visual. Which is the better choice?
  A) A map of Puerto Rico with Ponce marked in the south.
  B) A photograph of a beach.

Write A or B.

steps: The student is describing a location: where Ponce is on the island of Puerto Rico.
Option A (map with Ponce marked) shows exactly where the town is — matching the description.
Option B (beach photo) shows a beach but not where Ponce is located.
When a description is about location, a map is the best visual.

items.prompt:
A student is telling his class about penguins. He says: 'Penguins live in cold places like Antarctica. They have black backs and white bellies, and they walk in a funny waddling way.'

He wants to add a visual. Which is the better choice?
  A) A photograph of penguins showing their black-and-white coloring and their waddling posture.
  B) A photograph of a tropical rainforest.

Write A or B.

steps: The student described the penguin's appearance (black back, white belly) and how it moves (waddling).
Option A shows penguins with their actual colors and posture — matching everything in the description.
Option B shows a rainforest, which is the opposite climate from Antarctica.
The visual should show what the words described.

items.prompt:
A student is describing her classroom library. She says: 'Our class library has books organized by color on five shelves. The bottom shelf has picture books, the middle shelves have chapter books, and the top shelf has nonfiction.'

She wants to add a visual. Which is the better choice?
  A) A drawing of the five shelves showing which kind of books are on each shelf, with labels.
  B) A photograph of a bookstore.

steps: The student described the layout of the library: five shelves organized by type.
Option A (labeled drawing of the shelves) shows the layout described.
Option B (bookstore photo) shows a different place with a different organization.
A drawing of the specific shelves matches the description exactly.

items.prompt:
A student is recounting the experience of seeing a meteor shower. She says: 'We lay on blankets in the backyard and watched shooting stars. In the first hour we counted twelve. The best one had a long tail of light that lasted about three seconds.'

She wants to add a visual. Which is the better choice?
  A) A photograph of a daytime blue sky.
  B) A photograph of a night sky with visible shooting stars and light trails.

Write A or B.

steps: The student described a night sky with shooting stars and light trails.
Option B (night sky with shooting stars) shows exactly what was described.
Option A (daytime blue sky) shows the wrong time of day entirely.
The visual must match the scene being described.

items.prompt:
A student is explaining the parts of a plant. He says: 'A plant has roots underground, a stem, leaves, and flowers or fruit on top. The roots soak up water from the soil.'

He wants to add a visual. Which is the better choice?
  A) A labeled diagram of a plant showing the roots, stem, leaves, and flower.
  B) A photograph of a grocery store produce section.

Write A or B.

steps: The student described the parts of a plant, including roots underground.
Option A (labeled diagram) shows all the parts he named: roots, stem, leaves, flower.
Option B (grocery store) shows vegetables for sale, not the structure of a plant.
A diagram showing the parts matches the description and helps listeners see each part.

items.prompt:
A student is telling the class about a tradition her family celebrates. She says: 'Every year on Lunar New Year, my family makes dumplings together. We fold the dough around the filling and pinch the edges to seal them.'

She wants to add a visual. Which is the better choice?
  A) A photograph of someone's hands folding and pinching a dumpling closed.
  B) A photograph of fireworks.

Write A or B.

steps: The student described the specific action of folding and pinching dumplings.
Option A (hands folding a dumpling) shows exactly that action — helpful for a listener who has never made them.
Option B (fireworks) is related to Lunar New Year celebrations but not to the dumpling-making process the student described.
The visual should match what the student is specifically describing.

items.prompt:
A student is describing a caterpillar he found in his garden. He says: 'The caterpillar was bright green with yellow stripes and little black dots along each stripe. It was about two inches long.'

He wants to add a visual. Which is the better choice?
  A) A close-up photograph of the caterpillar showing its green color, yellow stripes, and black dots.
  B) A photograph of a butterfly.

Write A or B.

steps: The student is describing a specific caterpillar's appearance: color, stripes, dots, and length.
Option A shows the caterpillar he described — the listener can see the green, yellow, and black dots.
Option B shows a butterfly, which is what a caterpillar becomes later, not what was described.
The visual should show the subject of the description as it currently is.

  A) A photograph or drawing of the bake sale table with treats and the price poster above it.

Write A or B.

steps: The student described the bake sale setup: treats on a table, a price poster above.

items.prompt:
A student is describing how to play his favorite board game. He says: 'Each player picks a colored piece and puts it on Start. You roll the dice and move that many spaces. If you land on a red space you pick a card. The first person to reach Finish wins.'

He wants to add a visual. Which is the better choice?
  A) A photograph of the actual game board showing Start, the colored spaces, and Finish.
  B) A photograph of a playing card deck.

Write A or B.

steps: The student described the board game: Start, colored spaces, red spaces with cards, Finish.
Option A (game board photo) shows all of those features — the listener can see the layout.
Option B (playing cards) is a different game entirely and does not show the board game described.
When describing a board game, showing the board is the most helpful visual.

items.prompt:
A student is telling the class about her favorite recipe: mango smoothies. She says: 'You need frozen mango, yogurt, a little honey, and orange juice. You put everything in the blender and blend until smooth.'

She wants to add a visual. Which is the better choice?
  A) A photograph of all four ingredients (frozen mango, yogurt, honey, orange juice) laid out next to a blender.
  B) A photograph of a mango tree.

Write A or B.

steps: The student listed the four ingredients and described using a blender.
Option A shows all four ingredients and a blender — everything mentioned in the description.
Option B shows a mango tree, which is where mangoes come from but has nothing to do with making a smoothie.
A visual that shows the ingredients and tools matches the recipe description.

items.prompt:
A student is sharing the experience of watching a baby bird leave the nest. He says: 'A robin had built a nest in our maple tree. One morning I watched a baby bird stand on the edge, flap its wings for a long time, and then fly across the yard to a fence post.'

He wants to add a visual. Which is the better choice?
  A) A drawing of the baby robin on the nest's edge, the path of its flight shown with an arrow, and the fence post where it landed.
  B) A photograph of an empty nest.

Write A or B.

steps: The student described a flight path: from the nest in the tree, across the yard, to a fence post.
Option A (drawing with arrow) shows the path of the bird's flight — a journey with a starting and ending point.
Option B (empty nest) shows just the nest, not the flight or the destination.
When a description includes a movement or journey, a drawing with an arrow can show the path.
